Airtable vs Excel: Which Should You Use?

Excel is a true spreadsheet for calculations and analysis; Airtable is a database with spreadsheet looks, built for organizing and linking records. Use Excel for numbers, Airtable for structured data and workflows. Here is how they compare.

By The GridDojo Team Published August 4, 2026 2 min read

Airtable looks like a spreadsheet, so people naturally compare it to Excel — but under the hood they are different tools. Excel is a true spreadsheet built for calculations and analysis. Airtable is a database dressed as a spreadsheet, built for organizing, linking, and collaborating on records. The right choice depends on whether your job is mostly math or mostly structure.

Quick comparison

Airtable vs Excel at a glance
ExcelAirtable
Best atCalculations, analysis, big datasetsOrganizing and linking records
FormulasDeep spreadsheet functionsSimpler, per-field formulas
Field typesMostly text and numbersAttachments, checkboxes, links, more
ViewsThe gridGrid, kanban, calendar, gallery
Works offlineYes, desktop appLimited, cloud-based

When Excel wins

Choose Excel when the work is fundamentally about numbers: budgets, financial models, data cleanup, statistics, or anything with thousands of rows. Its formula engine, pivot tables, and charts go far beyond Airtable, and it stays fast with large datasets while working offline. If you want the classic spreadsheet done well, Excel is the tool.

When Airtable wins

Choose Airtable when you are organizing information rather than crunching it — a content calendar, a project tracker, an inventory, or a light CRM. Its rich field types (attachments, checkboxes, links between tables) and views like kanban and calendar make it far more pleasant than a spreadsheet for structured, collaborative work.

Tip: A simple rule: if you mostly calculate, use Excel. If you mostly organize and link records that a team updates together, use Airtable.

Who each is not for

  • Airtable is not for heavy calculations, large datasets, or advanced analysis — a spreadsheet handles those far better.
  • Excel is not the most pleasant tool for team databases with rich fields and multiple views — that is Airtable's strength. Comparing Airtable to the free option instead? See Airtable vs Google Sheets.
  • Still deciding between the big spreadsheets first? Read Excel vs Google Sheets.

Frequently asked questions

Is Airtable a replacement for Excel?

Not for real spreadsheet work. Airtable is great for organizing and linking records, but it lacks Excel's depth in formulas, pivot tables, and large-dataset performance. For calculations and analysis, Excel remains the better tool.

Can Airtable do formulas like Excel?

Airtable has formulas, but they work per field within a record, not across a grid of cells like Excel. They handle simple calculations well, not the multi-cell formulas and functions Excel is built for.

Is Airtable better than Excel for project management?

Usually yes. Airtable's linked records, kanban and calendar views, and rich field types make it a stronger fit for tracking projects, while Excel is better when the project is really about numbers and calculations.
